To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Americans discount future rewards more steeply than Koreans, and the difference in discounting is related to differences in emotional responsivity, but not to cognitive control.

(1) Americans discount the value of future rewards more than Koreans, (2) this is reflected in the greater activation of the ventral striatal reward region in Americans relative to Korean, but not in the greater activation in the prefrontial cortex, (3) these findings have important implications for the understanding of the strategic interaction between Westerners and Koreans.

Americans and Koreans differed significantly in their discounting behaviour, and this difference was related to the activation in the ventral striata, but not in the prefrontals and parietals, of the subjects.
